newsitem.title: USA: NFMA offers disclosure guide on muni housing bonds.
newsitem.headline: NFMA offers disclosure guide on muni housing bonds.

text.p: Municipal bond analysts on Monday called on issuers to adopt voluntary guidelines aimed at filling what they see as a gaping hole in secondary market information in the complex world of housing bonds.

"The secondary market for housing bonds (lacks) so much important bond redemption information, not to mention even the most rudimentary level of financial information, such as loan underwriting standards and building audits," the National Federation of Municipal Analysts (MFMA) warned in a 10-page packet.
Unless the housing bond sector adopts the recommendations, it will continue to experience "bond pricing penalties" that have plagued it for years, the draft guidelines say.
"It's not just us being persnickety," Mary Metastasio, head of NFMA's disclosure committee and coordinator of the guidelines project, said in a telephone interview. "There's no pet peve here."
She said following the guidelines should lower interest costs for issuers.

The standards come less than a week after the Association of Local Housing Finance Agencies issued its own draft guidelines on how local agencies can avoid liability under the Securities and Exchange Commission municipal disclosure and antifraud standards.

Metastasio said a panel of buy-side and sell-side analysts nationwide spent two years developing the draft standards, which apply to both single- and multi-family bonds issued by states and localities.
She said it is the first new set of disclosure recommendations made by the analysts' group since NFMA published a sector-by-sector disclosure handbook several years ago.
A vice president at SAFECO Asset Management in Seattle, Metastasio said NFMA prefers not to release the names of panel participants. Comments on the draft are requested by Sept. 15.

The draft guidelines cover five areas: disclosure for multi-family issues that predate SEC Rule 15c2-12, which sets minimum levels of disclosure; disclosure for new multi-family issues that lack loan underwriting information; tax law considerations; single-family program information; and general disclosure-related issues.
Comments should be sent to NFMA, P.O. Box 14893, Pittsburgh, Pa. 15234. Fax: 412-341-4894. Contact Mestastasio at 206-545-5736.
